Why two Part VII names share a key

Source: R/names.R
name_match_basis.Rd

For every person who appears on both the donor's and the recipient's Part VII (the same PERSON_KEY in one merger case), compares the raw first names on the two sides and records the basis of the match:

Usage

name_match_basis(part7)

Arguments

part7

The part7 table from build_merger_data() or merger_part7().

Value

A data.table, one row per merger case and shared person: MERGER_ID, PERSON_KEY, DONOR_FIRST, RECIP_FIRST (raw first names, ;; -separated when several), DONOR_NAMES, RECIP_NAMES, MATCH_BASIS, and REVIEW (TRUE for indirect, misspelling, and sound_alike).

Details

  • exact: the same first name appears on both sides;

  • nickname, spelling, cognate, compound: the two first names are a reviewed pair in peopleparser::first_name_pairs (BOB / ROBERT, STEVEN / STEPHEN, JUAN / JOHN, MARYANN / MARY ANN);

  • misspelling, sound_alike: an unreviewed pair in the same table (AAREN / AARON);

  • indirect: the names share a canonical form but are not a direct pair, for example a nickname of one spelling and the other spelling (KATIE / CATHERINE through KATHERINE). These are the ones to check by hand.

With the "simple" key every match is exact or indirect (the simple key ignores first names after the first token, so indirect there means the raw first names differ).
